question: Why do physics-informed neural networks often stop at high residual error despite extensive first-order training, and can a curvature-aware optimizer reliably finish the solve?

key_findings.claim: Low PDE solution error requires driving the composite PINN loss much closer to zero than common first-order optimizers typically achieve.
key_findings.evidence: Across convection, reaction, and wave equations and multiple widths/seeds, final relative solution error correlates strongly with residual/boundary loss. Adam or L-BFGS alone frequently stalls, while sequential Adam plus L-BFGS is a stronger baseline but remains under-optimized.

anchors.section: Loss versus L2 relative error / Figure 2

key_findings.claim: Differential operators create highly ill-conditioned curvature, explaining slow progress of scalar-step first-order methods near useful solutions.
key_findings.evidence: Empirical Hessian spectra separate loss components by scale, and the theoretical analysis links the PINN Gauss-Newton/tangent operator to the PDE differential operator. Eigenvalue decay yields large effective condition numbers under stated regularity and width assumptions.

key_findings.claim: Nyström Newton-CG materially reduces the residual after the Adam-plus-L-BFGS baseline and improves solution error on all three main PDEs.
key_findings.evidence: NNCG uses a randomized low-rank Nyström approximation as a preconditioner and conjugate-gradient Hessian solves. Figure 4 and Table 2 report more than a tenfold loss reduction in every displayed instance, whereas matched gradient-descent fine-tuning largely fails to move.

key_findings.claim: The optimizer improves accuracy at a substantial per-iteration cost, and the theory is local/conditional rather than a guarantee that arbitrary PINNs reach the right PDE solution.
key_findings.evidence: The timing appendix reports NNCG iterations several times slower than L-BFGS, while the convergence proof assumes local PL-like geometry, wide networks, damping, and sufficiently accurate curvature approximations. Function-class and collocation error remain separate from optimization error.

method.core_idea: Diagnose PINN failure as curvature ill-conditioning induced by differential residuals, then use a low-rank preconditioned second-order phase to finish optimization after robust first-order warm starts.
method.mechanism: The study compares optimizer sequences, measures Hessian and component spectra, relates infinite-width Gauss-Newton curvature to the PDE operator, and implements Nyström Newton-CG: randomized Hessian-vector sketches build a low-rank preconditioner, and damped conjugate gradient approximately solves each Newton system.
assumptions: Collocation losses and boundary terms faithfully represent the PDE solution within the chosen network class.
Hessian-vector products and Nyström sketches are accurate enough to expose the dominant stiff directions.
The first-order warm start enters a local region satisfying the proof's smoothness and PL-style conditions.
The benchmark PDEs and dense collocation grids represent the optimization pathologies encountered in larger scientific systems.

techniques.role: Measures curvature scale and condition across PDE-loss components.
Provides a strong first-order/quasi-Newton warm-start baseline.
Approximates dominant Hessian eigenspaces using matrix-vector products.
Uses iterative curvature solves to reduce the residual beyond first-order plateaus.
Connects PINN curvature conditioning to the underlying differential operator.

evaluations.setting: Convection, reaction, and wave PINNs across network widths, seeds, and tuned Adam/L-BFGS schedules.
evaluations.metric: Training loss and L2 relative solution error.
evaluations.result: Adam plus L-BFGS is consistently stronger than either alone, but many runs remain at losses high enough to cause visible solution error.
evaluations.baseline: Adam alone, L-BFGS alone, and tuned sequential Adam plus L-BFGS.

evaluations.setting: Post-warm-start fine-tuning on the three PDEs.
evaluations.result: NNCG reduces loss by more than an order of magnitude in each displayed case and improves L2RE; plain GD makes little progress from the same checkpoints.
evaluations.baseline: Gradient-descent fine-tuning and the original Adam-plus-L-BFGS checkpoint.

evaluations.setting: Empirical and theoretical Hessian conditioning analyses.
evaluations.metric: Spectral density, condition estimates, and convergence-rate dependence on curvature.
evaluations.result: Preconditioning compresses the stiff spectrum, while operator arguments predict severe conditioning for relevant differential losses under the stated assumptions.

limitations: The experimental suite is a small set of canonical PDEs with dense automatic differentiation, not large three-dimensional multiphysics.
NNCG requires extra Hessian-vector products, storage, and tuning, with materially slower iterations.
Local optimization theory assumes wide networks and regularity/PL properties that are not verified globally.
Low residual does not by itself certify uniform solution error between collocation points or uniqueness of the selected PDE solution.
failure_modes: A poor first-order checkpoint may lie outside the local basin where Newton-CG is stable.
An undersized Nyström sketch can miss important stiff directions and yield ineffective or indefinite steps.
Unbalanced boundary and residual terms can make curvature improvement optimize the wrong composite objective.
Collocation aliasing can produce a low sampled residual while retaining large continuous-domain error.
reusable_insights: Report both final residual loss and solution error; optimizer comparisons at a fixed loose loss can be misleading.
Differential-operator spectra predict optimizer stiffness and can guide preconditioner design.
A staged optimizer—cheap global progress followed by selective curvature solves—is a practical pattern for scientific ML.
open_questions: Can structured PDE preconditioners replace costly generic Nyström sketches in high dimensions?
How should curvature methods jointly adapt residual, boundary, and data-loss weights?
Can continuous-domain certificates distinguish optimization error from collocation and approximation error during training?

competitive_landscape.title: An Expert's Guide to Training Physics-informed Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Provides reproducible architecture and optimizer best practices plus difficult PINN benchmarks.
competitive_landscape.difference: It emphasizes a broad recipe of first-order training improvements; this paper centers on Hessian conditioning and a specific randomized second-order solver.

competitive_landscape.title: Efficient Error Certification for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Addresses whether a trained PINN has uniformly small continuous-domain PDE residual rather than only low sampled error.
competitive_landscape.difference: It is a post-training certification framework; the loss-landscape paper improves optimization but does not supply worst-case residual guarantees.

competitive_landscape.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks with Learnable Loss Balancing and Transfer Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Targets PINN instability through adaptive weighting between physics and data terms plus transfer.
competitive_landscape.difference: It changes the objective weighting and initialization source; this paper treats curvature ill-conditioning of a fixed PINN loss with preconditioned second-order optimization.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: PINN training difficulty is explained by differential-operator-induced ill-conditioning, and Nyström Newton-CG overcomes plateaus left by Adam and L-BFGS.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Spectral measurements, operator theory, matched post-checkpoint fine-tuning, and consistent loss/L2RE gains support the account on three PDE classes.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The mechanistic link and strong optimization baseline are valuable; general utility depends on amortizing curvature cost and validating continuous-domain correctness at larger scale.

reviewer_notes: Read the complete 33-page paper including timing, operator-spectrum, and local-convergence appendices. Training and certification competitors were checked at primary arXiv pages on 2026-08-23.
